STEP 1 - Scene: This is a bowl of dark red grapes (not a full meal), photographed from above at a near top-down angle, sitting on a glass/wooden surface.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The bowl is a white/light cereal-style bowl, roughly 15 cm in diameter. Area = 3.14 x (7.5)^2 ≈ 177 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: One food: red seedless grapes, heaped in the bowl.

STEP 4 - Area: Grapes fill essentially the whole bowl opening, about 90% of the vessel area.

STEP 5 - Volume: The pile is about 4 cm deep on average (heaped above the rim slightly). 177 cm^2 x 0.9 x 4 cm ≈ 640 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Grapes are whole fruit with gaps, bulk density ~0.65 g/ml. 640 x 0.65 ≈ 415 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Grapes ~69 kcal per 100 g. 415 g x 0.69 ≈ 286 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 40 grapes at roughly 8 g each is about 320 g, consistent with ~400 g. A bowl of grapes at 400 g and ~285 kcal is plausible for a full cereal bowl. Estimate is a bit high on the density side, so I'll settle at about 380 g.

Revised: 380 g x 0.69 ≈ 262 kcal.
